title: A story in five minutes
description: Five minutes is enough for a complete tiny story if you borrow a simple shape: someone wants something, something gets in the way.

body.heading: Borrow a simple shape
paragraphs: Long stories have room to wander; tiny ones need a spine. Use this one: a character wants something small and specific, tries to get it, meets one obstacle, and ends slightly changed.
The want can be tiny. A cat wants the sunny spot on the sofa. A lighthouse keeper wants one quiet evening. Small wants make charming stories.

body.heading: Write it in three bursts
paragraphs: Spend one minute on the opening: who, where, and what they want. Spend three minutes on the attempt and the obstacle. Spend the last minute on the ending, even if it is just one line.
Do not aim for polish. Aim for finished. A complete rough story teaches you more than the perfect first paragraph of an unfinished one, and you can always write another tomorrow.

takeaway: One want, one obstacle, five minutes: a whole story, done.
